__doc__: Old-canon debt ratchet for scripts/verify-conform.mjs check 1 (CORE-116).
Each entry is a file that still carries references to the pre-ADR-0001 install
canon — a hardcoded kit home, the dead ~/Desktop/my-assistant workspace, or the
dead .first-run-pending marker — together with how many references it has TODAY.
These are not exemptions. The count may only go DOWN: a file over its number, or
any file not listed here, fails the check. Files listed here belong to sibling
ADR-0001 tickets that had not merged when this ratchet was set: CORE-113 (the
trimmed persona, my-assistant/CLAUDE.md), CORE-114 (first-run-setup -> orientation)
and CORE-117 (the stale-doc sweep across docs/, skills/, visuals/, README,
whatsapp-channel). As each lands, run `node scripts/verify-conform.mjs
--update-baseline` and commit the shrunken file. When it is empty, delete it.
Permanently-legitimate surfaces (migration, uninstall, the ADR, the fixtures) are
NOT here — they are in OLD_CANON_ALLOWLIST, and docs/start/setup.md is scoped by
section rather than allowlisted at all.
Known holes, so nobody reads a green ratchet as more than it is:
1. A line is counted ONCE PER PATTERN, not per occurrence — three hardcoded
homes on one line count as one. Rewrapping a baselined file can therefore
change its count without changing its meaning; re-snapshot rather than
arguing with the number.
2. The count is per file, so a same-file SWAP is invisible: delete one old-canon
reference and add a different one in the same file and the total holds. The
ratchet catches accumulation, not substitution. Reviewers still read diffs.
3. `--update-baseline` snapshots the tree as it is, with NO gate — it will
happily record new debt. It is a maintenance command for after a sweep lands,
not a way to make a failing check pass. A raised number in this file is a
reviewable diff, and that is the whole enforcement.
